rationale: The compiled case faithfully implements the design and the assigned route MESSAGE→REACTION→USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP inside a single selector, matching the referent entity (messages) and correctly returning the two expected matches (1699564800.000123 for Robert Walsh, 1706000208.000000 for Robert Chen) with candidate_role_sets mirroring the two alternative interpretations, consistent with resolution_mode=underspecified since neither the prompt nor any role delegates a choice between the two same-named Roberts. The reactor_workspace_role obligation intentionally reports both membership rows (admin for Walsh, member for Chen) as a fixed pair rather than mirroring the message alternatives — this is explicitly sanctioned by the case's own exposure_qualification ('report the displayed membership pair'), so it is not an inconsistency. All match, alternative, and negative rows are grounded in pre-existing base-seed messages/users (e.g., 1700173200.000456 authored by and reacted 'eyes' by Robert Walsh; 1706067472.000000 authored by and reacted 'heart' by Robert Chen; 1706012456.000000 reacted 'thumbsup' by Sophie Dubois) and the new message_reactions rows inserted by the compiler are the only additions needed, correctly reflecting planned writer intent. Mechanical checks show computed_matches equal to the two expected messages and near-misses correctly separated by emoji-value and name-condition, with no reported errors. Access is realistic: the acting bot already had membership in nearly every needed channel, and the two added channel_members rows (C_GROWTH, C_OLD_PROJECT) support legitimate discovery completeness without granting any unsupported capability. Answer attributes (messages.message_text/channel_id/user_id, user_teams.role) are bare stored columns, and identifying paths correctly traverse entity/edge sequences rather than encoding literal predicates. The case is a strong test of ambiguous-referent handling with well-motivated, non-hinting negatives (wrong emoji from the same reactor, and correct emoji from the wrong person) and a real multi-hop join across workspace membership, exceeding bare single-hop retrieval.
